title: Week 10
description: Fog Computing, Smart Cities and Smart Homes

questions.question: In the analogy comparing humans to smart cities presented in the lecture, what do 'Sensors and Tags' correspond to?
Which of the following is listed as one of the six 'Application Focus Areas' of a smart city?
Under 'Current Focus Areas' of smart cities, which application area specifically deals with the auto routing of vehicles to empty slots and detecting vacant slots?
Which IoT challenge in smart cities relates to the risk of data leakage arising from multiple tenants sharing the same infrastructure?
What is the primary purpose of data fusion in IoT-enabled smart city environments, as described in the lecture?
options: To delete redundant sensors from the network
To make the large incoming data volume precise and accurate for better decision making
To replace the need for any sensors

questions.question: Which data fusion challenge refers to the situation where the same type of sensor reports different data for the same location?
In the stages of data fusion, at which level does the fusion of information happen at the sensor node or within the local network itself?
Which of the following is listed as one of the three functional layers of a smart parking system?
In the classification of energy harvesting solutions for smart cities, which type involves energy sources intentionally deployed near IoT devices?
Which Home Area Network (HAN) standard is defined by IEEE 802.15.4 at the physical and MAC layers, and aims at low-cost, low-energy devices?
Which HAN standard enables remote control of compliant devices over existing power lines and electrical wiring in a house, and is mainly used for lighting and appliance control?
According to the lecture, why does traditional TCP/IP fail to work well for Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication?
options: TCP/IP was designed mainly for single-pair information exchange dependent on data location
TCP/IP cannot be used with any wireless devices
TCP/IP requires no IP addresses at all
TCP/IP works only in stationary networks with no scalability limits

questions.question: Which frequency spectrum did the US Department of Transport and FCC allocate for Intelligent Connected Vehicles (ICVs)?
In the phases of ICV development described in the lecture, which phase is based on 4G LTE or DSRC and focuses on intelligent transportation services?
In the VANET domain classification, which domain consists of vehicles (mobile) and Road-Side Units (RSUs, static), communicating via V2V or V2I using the DSRC stack?
